title: What is CATZOC and why does it matter to navigators?

scenes.label: MARITIME TERM OF THE DAY
scenes.heading: Your chart could be wrong by 500 metres.
scenes.narration: A sounding on your chart could be several metres out, and its position wrong by five hundred. CATZOC tells you how far to trust it.

scenes.heading: CATZOC
scenes.narration: CATZOC stands for Category of Zone of Confidence. It is the quality rating of the survey data behind every part of an electronic chart.

scenes.label: SURVEY QUALITY
scenes.heading: How well was the seabed surveyed?
scenes.narration: In a zone rated A1, the whole seabed was surveyed and significant features were found and measured. In zone C, coverage was only partial, so depth anomalies may be expected.

scenes.label: DEPTH ACCURACY AT 20 m
scenes.heading: Same sounding, different trust
scenes.narration: The difference is large. At a charted depth of twenty metres, A1 data is accurate to about seventy centimetres. In zone C, the same sounding may be three metres out.

scenes.label: ON THE BRIDGE
scenes.heading: Build it into your UKC
scenes.body: Check the CATZOC of every shallow leg of the passage and add its depth error to your under-keel clearance margin.
scenes.narration: So when you plan a passage, check the CATZOC of every shallow leg, and add that possible error to your under keel clearance calculation.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: A chart is only as good as its survey.
scenes.narration: Remember: a chart is only as good as the survey behind it.

meta.description: CATZOC (Category of Zone of Confidence) tells the navigator how accurate the survey data behind an ENC really is. Here is what the categories A1 to D mean and how to use them in passage planning and UKC calculations.
